cohort: 260 Brazilian women aged 19-43 years in the postpartum period
finding: A higher dietary inflammatory index (E-DII) was associated with lower adherence to physical activity during pregnancy, a higher frequency of cesarean delivery, increased maternal body mass index over time, and changes in the lipid profile of human milk, specifically higher fat content by the third month postpartum.
mod_finding: Women with a higher dietary inflammatory index (E-DII) had a higher frequency of cesarean delivery.
